name: Shesha
role: Cosmic serpent who bears the world and Vishnu's couch
summary: Shesha, also called Ananta, is the many-hooded serpent on whom Vishnu rests. Puranic texts say he holds up worlds on his hoods and remains when everything else dissolves.
about: Shesha means 'remainder', because the Puranas say he is what endures when the universe dissolves at the end of a cycle; he is also called Ananta, 'endless'. The Mahabharata names him the eldest of the thousand serpents born to Kashyapa and Kadru. Disturbed by his siblings' ways, he is said to have left them and prayed in places such as Gokarna and Pushkara. Many Puranas say that Brahma granted him a boon and asked him to carry the Earth from below, so he supports it on his hood in Patala. Vaishnava traditions count him among Vishnu's closest companions, along with Garuda, and describe a form called Samkarshana. Different traditions say he returned as Lakshmana, as Balarama, as the grammarian Patanjali, as Ramanuja, or as Nityananda.
kidSummary: Shesha is a giant, gentle serpent in Hindu stories. He has many hoods that make a soft, wide bed for Vishnu to rest on, and he is also said to hold up the worlds. His name means what is left at the very end of everything.

story.title: A different kind of serpent
story.text: Shesha was the eldest of a thousand serpent brothers and sisters. In the Mahabharata, he did not like how some of them behaved, so he left to meditate in quiet places like Gokarna and Pushkara.

story.title: A wish for goodness
story.text: Brahma was pleased with Shesha's prayers and offered him a boon. Shesha asked only that his mind stay steady in what is right and in devotion.

story.title: Holding up the Earth
story.text: Brahma then asked Shesha to carry the Earth from beneath. Shesha went to the world below, called Patala, and has held up the Earth on his hood ever since.

story.title: Vishnu's resting place
story.text: Vishnu is shown resting on Shesha's coils. With a thousand hoods and a thousand mouths, he is said to sing Vishnu's praises without end.

story.title: A shelter in the storm
story.text: Tales of Krishna's birth say that when Vasudeva carried the baby across the stormy Yamuna, Shesha followed and spread his hoods over them like an umbrella.

story.title: Returning as helpers
story.text: Later stories say Shesha came back to earth as Lakshmana, loyal brother of Rama, and again as Balarama, elder brother of Krishna.

teaches: Steady devotion to what is right
Staying calm and patient through change

facts.text: The name Shesha means roughly 'remainder', since the Puranas say he alone endures when the universe dissolves; as Ananta, he is 'the endless one'.
In pictures he usually has five, seven or ten hoods, but old texts imagine a full thousand heads, each wearing a crown.
The Brahma Purana pictures Ananta with a thousand hoods, a thousand shining jewels, a single earring, blue clothes, a plough and an iron club.
The Brahmanda Purana describes Shesha in Patala as pale as the moon, with two thousand eyes that glow like the rising sun, and a resting body like a thousand-peaked mountain.
In the sanctum of Padmanabhaswamy Temple, devotees see the reclining Vishnu through three doors. Brahma sits on a lotus from his navel, which gives the form its name Padmanabha.
In temple art Shesha often forms a hooded canopy. At Vijayanagara, Narasimha sits on his coils beneath seven heads, and at Bhubaneswar a five-headed Shesha shelters Vishnu.
Shesha has a gayatri-style mantra of his own that calls on him as Sheshanaga and Ananta and asks the naga to inspire the mind.
Tradition names Shesha's wife as Nagalakshmi, whom the Garga Samhita describes as the Ocean of Milk itself. She is said to have been born as Urmila, Sita's sister, when Shesha came as Lakshmana.
In Sri Vaishnava belief, Shesha appeared in the Satya Yuga as a seat for Narasimha after the defeat of Hiranyakashipu.
Sri Vaishnavas say Shesha returned in the Kali Yuga as the grammarian Patanjali and as the teacher Ramanuja, while Gaudiya Vaishnavas say he came as Nityananda.
A statue of the sage Patanjali shows him in snake form, which is said to stand for kundalini energy or for being an incarnation of Shesha.
The Brahma Purana says that at the end of time, Rudra in the form of Samkarshana comes out of Shesha's mouth and burns the three worlds with fiery poison.
At Padmanabhaswamy Temple in Thiruvananthapuram, Vishnu reclines on five-hooded Ananta. The idol is made of 12,008 saligram stones from Nepal's Gandaki river.
The Palliyodam snake boat at Kerala's Aranmula is traditionally said to have been designed by Krishna to look like Shesha.
In Thai folk religion Shesha is revered as a major naga, second only to Grandfather Sri Sutho Naga of Kham Chanod. A shrine to him stands under the Second Thai-Lao Friendship Bridge in Mukdahan.

A relief from Mathura dated to the 1st or 2nd century CE seems to show Vasudeva carrying baby Krishna across the Yamuna beside a seven-hooded naga, an image many link with the tale of Shesha sheltering the baby.

Some scriptures say a great white snake left Balarama's mouth when he departed the world, showing he was Ananta Shesha. Locals near Somnath point to a cave where it is said to have gone down to Patala.
Ananta Chaturdashi, when Vishnu's Ananta form is honoured, is also the last day of the ten-day Ganesh Chaturthi festival, when Ganesha idols are immersed in water.

In the Mahabharata tale behind Ananta Chaturdashi, Kaundinya throws his wife's sacred thread into a fire and loses everything. He finds Ananta, is forgiven, and is asked to keep the vow for fourteen years.
In the Bhagavata Purana, Ananta, the thousand-headed serpent, is foretold to be born ahead of Krishna as his elder brother, to please Hari.

quiz.q: What does the name Shesha roughly mean?
quiz.why: He is what remains when the universe dissolves at the end of a cycle.

quiz.q: Who rests on Shesha's coils in many Hindu stories?
In the Treta Yuga, many traditions say Shesha was born as whom?
quiz.why: Lakshmana, Rama's brother, is said to be Shesha reborn.

quiz.q: What are the Padmanabhaswamy Temple's idol stones called?
quiz.why: The idol is made of 12,008 saligram stones from the Gandaki river.

quiz.q: What did Shesha ask for when Brahma offered a boon?
quiz.why: He asked that his mind stay on righteousness and devotion.

quiz.why: The Palliyodam used at Aranmula is said to have been designed by Krishna to resemble Shesha.
